newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO general, Israeli religious party sage meet.
newsitem.headline: PLO general, Israeli religious party sage meet.

text.p: Palestinian police chief Nasr Yousef met on Friday the spiritual leader of a key member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's ruling coalition to discuss stalled Israeli-PLO peace moves.

Major-General Yousef, commander of the Palestinian security forces in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, called his 45-minute talks in West Jerusalem with Shas party mentor Rabbi Ovadia Yosef as "excellent and very friendly."
The meeting was seen as part of the Palestinian Authority's efforts to pressure Netanyahu to implement self-rule deals signed with Israel's previous Labour government.
"The rabbi agreed that it was dangerous to go back on agreements that have been signed," Yousef told Reuters.

He said they also agreed to work to prevent a recurrence of last month's violence in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed as a result of gunbattles and stone-throwing clashes, the worst bloodshed in the West Bank and Gaza since PLO rule began there in 1994.
No Shas officials were immediately available to comment on the report.

It was the second time that Palestinian officials met leaders of Shas, which generally supported peace moves by Israel's former Labour government and is considered among the more moderate of the Jewish state's largely religious parties.

Israeli-PLO talks on implementing parts of the self-rule agreement began on Sunday but have yet to yield results. Israel is demanding changes in one accord calling for Israeli army redeployment in Hebron.
The redeployment agreements were concluded with the governments of slain prime minister Yitzhak Rabin and his successor Shimon Peres, defeated by Netanyahu in May elections.

On Thursday, Mahmoud Abbas, known as Abu Mazen, a senior member of the executive committee of the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) met Shas head Aryeh Deri and Haim Ramon, a leader of the main opposition Labour party.
"The meeting centred on the political situation, on political negotiations, on what will happen in the future...It is important that these meetings take place," Ramon told Israel Radio on Thursday.
